public_rationale: Nebius's October 22 disclosure describes a corporate facility initially priced at Term SOFR plus 2.75%, with proceeds for data centers, GPUs and general corporate purposes [e1]. It does not establish a qualifying project financing with verified all-in costs and no direct hyperscaler backstop [e1]. Digi Power X's October 13 announcement describes a conditional $200 million commitment without an interest rate or confirmation of closing [e2]. Neither disclosure establishes the guaranteed 9–14% range, supplies a qualifying counterexample or shows that debt service makes viable operation nearly unattainable [e1, e2].
limitations: Neither disclosure conclusively verifies the absence of direct hyperscaler credit support.
No completed qualifying financing has a verified all-in annual rate.
No project cash-flow evidence establishes the claimed economic consequence.
The forecast has no deadline; a few transactions within the range would not establish a universal guarantee.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data center projects not backstopped by hyperscalers will face 9-14% rates, making data center economics near-impossible to work.
conditions: projects not backstopped or co-signed by hyperscalers

statement.excerpt: This means that any “virgin” projects — those that aren’t directly backstopped or co-signed by hyperscalers — are guaranteed to hit egregiously-high, 9% to 14% rates, which makes (as I discussed a few weeks ago in my two-part debt series) it near-impossible to make the already-questionable economics of running a data center work.

from_speaker: aren’t directly backstopped or co-signed by hyperscalers
economics of running a data center
our_interpretation: The qualifying condition is a new AI data center project financing without a direct hyperscaler backstop or co-signature.
A hyperscaler customer alone does not establish a financing guarantee. Silence about guarantees does not prove their absence.
I read rates as all-in annual borrowing costs, including material discounts and fees, rather than the loan margin alone.
I assess financings after publication. The claim states no deadline.
Near-impossible economics means debt service makes commercially viable operation exceptionally difficult, not merely that financing is costly.
criteria.support_condition: Verified qualifying financings carry all-in annual rates of 9–14%, and representative project cash-flow evidence shows that these costs make viable operation nearly unattainable. A few conforming transactions cannot establish the universal guarantee.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed qualifying financing outside 9–14% supplies a counterexample to the guaranteed range. Demonstrated sustainable project economics can separately challenge the economic consequence.

evidence.explanation: The release discloses a short-term corporate facility priced against Term SOFR. Its mixed uses, unspecified all-in costs and incomplete backstop information prevent treating it as a qualifying counterexample.

evidence.locator: First sentence of CEO Michel Amar's quotation
evidence.publisher: Digi Power X via ACCESS Newswire
evidence.explanation: The release describes a conditional project financing commitment and a company completion guarantee. It does not disclose an interest rate, establish closing, or conclusively exclude other credit support.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Executed post-publication financing documents verifying project purpose, all guarantees, closing and all-in annual costs. A qualifying financing outside 9–14% would refute the universal rate assertion. Independently checkable project cash flows after operating costs, maintenance investment and debt service would test the economic consequence.
